title: EU AI Act Article 5 prohibited AI practices
description: Flags assets whose use case, calling service, data flows or detected PII resemble a practice prohibited by Article 5(1)(a)-(h) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (applicable since 2 February 2025). Every rule is level 'critical' so it sorts first, and every match is only a suggestion for a human (legal or compliance) to review: keyword signals cannot establish the legal conditions of a prohibition (for example 'significant harm', 'based solely on profiling', 'real-time', 'publicly accessible spaces') or its exceptions (medical or safety reasons in point (f), the law-enforcement objectives and authorisation in point (h) and Article 5(2)-(7)). Rule references quote the operative words of each point.

rules.reference: Article 5(1)(a): "deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques" materially distorting behaviour and causing significant harm
rules.title: Possible prohibited practice: subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques (human review required)

rules.reference: Article 5(1)(b): "exploits any of the vulnerabilities of a natural person or a specific group of persons due to their age, disability or a specific social or economic situation" materially distorting behaviour and causing significant harm
rules.title: Possible prohibited practice: exploiting vulnerabilities due to age, disability or social or economic situation (human review required)

rules.reference: Article 5(1)(c): "evaluation or classification of natural persons or groups of persons over a certain period of time based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal or personality characteristics" with the social score leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment
rules.title: Possible prohibited practice: social scoring (human review required)

rules.reference: Article 5(1)(d): risk assessments "to assess or predict the risk of a natural person committing a criminal offence, based solely on the profiling of a natural person or on assessing their personality traits and characteristics" (not support for a human assessment already based on objective and verifiable facts)
rules.title: Possible prohibited practice: predicting an individual's criminal offending from profiling or personality traits (human review required)

rules.reference: Article 5(1)(e): AI systems "that create or expand facial recognition databases through the untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage"
rules.title: Possible prohibited practice: untargeted scraping of facial images for facial recognition databases (human review required)

rules.reference: Article 5(1)(f): AI systems "to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions, except where the use of the AI system is intended to be put in place or into the market for medical or safety reasons"
rules.title: Possible prohibited practice: emotion recognition in the workplace or education (human review required)

rules.reference: Article 5(1)(g): biometric categorisation systems that categorise individually natural persons based on their biometric data "to deduce or infer their race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation" (does not cover labelling or filtering of lawfully acquired biometric datasets, or categorising biometric data in the area of law enforcement)
rules.title: Possible prohibited practice: biometric categorisation inferring sensitive traits (human review required)

rules.reference: Article 5(1)(h): "the use of 'real-time' remote biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces for the purposes of law enforcement", unless strictly necessary for one of the listed objectives
rules.title: Possible prohibited practice: real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement (human review required)
